description:
Ice Cream Stabilizers PT2 is about Tapioca Starch, Cornstarch, CMC, GMS and Tara Gum. 
If you want to know a little bit more on these ingredients, have a watch and ask any questions you might have and I will do my best to answer them. 

I'm not a chemist, just a guy who makes ice cream (albeit well) and likes to experiment with ingredient options. 

---------------------------

If you want to watch the PT1 of Ice Cream Stabilizers, check out this link:
https://youtu.be/GyTIS0ic3Qs?si=I5p4eGW4JSt40IHv

----------------------------

The stabilizer playlist is here:
https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQC4zsI_2FcHwB7kBla7tKcZ4o_NecSC6&si=8ihIfDtx2mc63wLV

-----------------------------

If you havn't already, make sure to head to the Community tab and vote on the Poll that's running where you can decide whats made on the channel.  

If you enjoyed this video, please consider liking, commenting and subscribing, plus pop over to our Instagram page linked below and say hello :)

Instagram: https://tinyurl.com/2p85zcxh
Facebook: Don't use it anymore, sorry. 
Website: https://www.polaricecreamery.com
Ko-Fi Link: https://ko-fi.com/icecreamery


Thanks and see you on the next video :)

comments.text:
Enjoy your video clips and watch them regularly. Great channel for ice cream makers.

Some questions: I use a combination of skimmed milk powder, inulin and a small quantity of egg (solids after heating - 73-75C for 20-30 minutes - are roughly 7%, 4% and 2% respectively) with a cream/milk liquid base when making ice cream. Sugar is 8-10% of solids, depending on flavour I'm making.

How do you rate inulin? For what purpose would you use it? If you do not normally use it, what do you prefer using in its place? 

Cheers!!
comments.author: @petercarver4126

comments.text:
Hi Peter. I don’t use inulin as it disagrees with me. There’s no need to use it either if you’re making dairy ice cream. Milk, cream, sugar, skimmed milk powder and the flavor are the only things you need really. 
Inulin is mainly used in plant based recipes to boost solids. It’s rarely used as sugar as it not particularly functional in that regard. What reason do you use it for out of curiosity?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: Good Question: Experimenting came across a recipe that have used successfully that included inulin. I looked up inulin in ice cream and - depending on type and DP value - it can lower sugar and fat content while maintaining similar mouth feel. Based on your comments, might try same recipe minus the inulin. BTW: Thanks for you swift reply and I enjoy watching your videos. They have given me some great insight into various ingredients used in making ice cream. Cheers,  @PolarIceCreamery
comments.author: @petercarver4126

comments.text: BTW: I have noticed thtat using inulin I have been able to reduce sugar and fat content while maintaining same/similar taste and mouth feel
comments.author: @petercarver4126

comments.text: @petercarver4126 that is a common use to be fair. The problem lies when it’s taken too far, inulin only works n this situation to a point. I’ll talk about n a large sugars video very soon.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: Thanks for reply. I use 4% or less of solids content. WIll try recipe using 1/2 the amount and without any to see what the results are. Cheers  @PolarIceCreamery
comments.author: @petercarver4126

comments.text: @petercarver4126   you can also start using dextrose or glucose to replace some of the sugar as it will make it softer and it's not a sweet (sugar alcohols are also an option much like inulin). Sugars are a big subject in ice cream, one I need to talk about in a big video.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: Wonderful information!   Thanks for letting us know about all of this!  So let me ask;  what stabilizer will produce the coldest yet smooth consistency in ice cream, and let’s say we’re talking about vanilla ice cream.
comments.author: @jonl.garton4616

comments.text: Well you actually don’t want it too cold, that’s a sign of too much free, unaccountable water in the ice cream. You’ll try some n some stores and you think “too cold” and someone will laugh and say ” well it’s ice cream!” But they don’t understand. Guar Gum+LBG+ Carrageenan is a time served combination, Tara gum is excellent, LBG n its own in a well balanced recipe is also excellent. For something like vanilla, start with Tara gum at 0.1% of the total recipe and go from there.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
Do you have any experience with polysorbate 80? Obviously it also very much pushes the proccesses boundaries, but it is supposed to be an astonishingly efficient emulsifier.
I aquired some and have used it for two batches.
The main thing i seemed to notice is I seem to be able to leave the batc in my compressor machine longer to get more over run without getting the greasy feel from fat coalescing due to over churning. 
Supposedly it also combines especially well with mono- and diglycerides, though I have not been able to aquire any to test.

Also do you have any thoughts on combining small amoubts of various gums to create synergistic effects between them?
comments.author: @JonathanGoggans

comments.text:
Synergistic combination is an excellent way to achieve a perfect result. That’s really what it’s all about! 
I personally don’t use Polysorbate 80 but it apparently combines well with lecithin too so might be worth a try if you fancy it 👍
